body: Sensex 21,206.77 (10 Jan 2008) to a closing low of ~8,160 (9 Mar 2009), -61.5%; intraday it touched ~7,700 on 27 Oct 2008 (from memory). Nifty 50 TRI -59% (calendar 2008); Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI -73%; Nifty Smallcap 100 intra-year fall -76%; the BSE Smallcap was -70.7% from its 52-week high by 17 Oct 2008. Sensex P/E more than halved, ~27x to ~11.9x (Business Standard; Morningstar says ~12). What led the fall: realty (DLF, Unitech -90%+), infra, capital goods, metals, small caps; what held up relatively: FMCG, pharma, IT. Bottom signals: P/E ~11-12x, record FII selling, IPO market shut, dividend yields ~2%, policy response (RBI rate cuts from Oct 2008, fiscal stimulus) and the May 2009 election result (Sensex upper circuit on 18 May 2009). Recovery: Sensex regained ~21,000 in Nov 2010 (about 34 months from peak) but did not sustain new highs until late 2013; the Nifty Smallcap 100 took ~69 months (Nov 2014, Value Research) and the BSE Smallcap until ~2017 to close above its Jan 2008 high; Smallcap 250 TRI >6 years (DSP). Entry before the crisis gave ~8% CAGR to Mar 2026 in Smallcap 250 TRI vs ~18% from the bottom. Lesson: buying small caps at cycle-peak valuations can cost 6+ years even when the long-run trend is up.

data.lesson: peak-valuation small caps can take 6+ yrs

title: 2008 global financial crisis crash in India
